clue.text: Two different ways Brewers may reveal pitcher

indicators.note: the letters can be read both forwards and backwards in Brewers, and this route reads them backwards
to reveal is to show what lies within, so the letters sit inside the word Brewers

explanation.surface: A beer drinker's remark that a brewery can serve up a jug in two ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters run forwards in bREWERs and also backwards in the reversal SREWERB; the parse shows the backwards route, but 'Two different ways' means both work.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug, and pitcher is the American word for a jug.

clue.text: Could I get lucky? On the surface a great deal

parts.note: could means might, as in 'it might rain'

indicators.note: the surface of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters of lucky are used

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether luck will come their way, though it looks like a big deal outwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' is a link word between the two halves of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mightily is an informal intensifier meaning very much or enormously, the same sense as a great deal.

clue.text: See 7
Tearful at first getting stick about one's muscles

indicators.note: about means around, so the glue goes around the letter picked from Tearful

parts.note: glue is something that sticks

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of Tearful

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone weeping as their muscles get stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts T (from 'Tearful at first') inside GLUE, making GLUTE, and then I for 'one' goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The glutei are the buttock muscles; this is the Latin plural of gluteus.

clue.text: Hairy bloke seen in the sauna

indicators.note: seen in says the letters are visible inside the words the sauna

explanation.surface: A man with lots of body hair spotted in the steam room.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau, brother of Jacob, is described as a hairy man.

clue.text: Pulls up with wife going, "It's not very far"

indicators.note: going means leaving, so the letter for wife is taken away

parts.note: winches means hauls up with a winch

explanation.surface: Someone hoisting a load while their wife leaves, saying it is a short way.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing W leaves the answer. The definition works as a phrase: if something is only a few of these away, it is not far.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a tiny unit of length, so a few of them make a very short distance.

clue.text: Terrible crime? Wrong — a blag! In the end was seen to be a non-event

indicators.note: terrible means badly made, so the letters that follow are rearranged
in the end takes only the final letter of was

explanation.surface: A dreadful robbery story that turned out never to have happened.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is CRIME, WRONG, A BLAG, S (the end of 'was') and SEEN; 'to be' is a link. Kellyanne Conway cited this 'massacre' in 2017 to defend a US travel ban; it never happened.
explanation.definitionFit: The supposed Bowling Green attack was invented in a TV interview, so it is a famous event that never took place.

clue.text: Suggest Bill possesses a sixth sense

indicators.note: possesses means holds within, so the beak wraps around the sixth sense

parts.note: a bird's bill is its beak
ESP, extrasensory perception, is called a sixth sense

explanation.surface: A hint that a man called Bill is psychic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but here it is a bird's bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To bespeak is to be evidence of or point to something, so it means to suggest or indicate.

clue.text: Looked surprised government's getting mocked

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for government
aped means mimicked, copying someone to mock them

explanation.surface: Someone astonished to see the government being ridiculed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link word joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to stare open-mouthed, which is how someone looks when they are astonished.

clue.text: Knackered crossing like this Liverpool footballer

indicators.note: crossing means lying across, so the phrase for exhausted goes around the words for like this

parts.note: knackered is British slang for exhausted, which is also 'all in'
so means in this way, as in 'do it so'

explanation.surface: An exhausted footballer, like this one from Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious candidate is Liverpool's goalkeeper Alisson Becker, though his name has one L and two S's; the grid spelling follows the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This names a player for Liverpool Football Club, presumably the Brazilian goalkeeper Alisson.

clue.text: Spokesperson struggling hard as answers lacking weight

indicators.note: struggling means in difficulty, so the letters are thrown into a new order
lacking means without, so the weight letter is taken out of answers

explanation.surface: A press officer having a hard time giving answers with no substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes W from ANSWERS, leaving ANSERS; 'struggling' rearranges HARD AS plus ANSERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Sanders was White House Press Secretary under Trump, the administration's chief spokeswoman.

clue.text: Stop it! Ultimately ridiculous woman's ignoring the facts

indicators.note: ridiculous means absurd, so stop plus that letter are jumbled
ultimately means finally, so only the closing letter of it is used

parts.note: Ruth is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea to a ridiculous woman who will not face reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' takes T from IT; 'ridiculous' rearranges STOP+T into POSTT; then add RUTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-truth describes a climate where emotion and belief count for more than objective evidence.

clue.text: Draw flag — that's not right

indicators.note: that's not says the right letter is missing, so it is removed

parts.note: to flag is to tire, to lose energy

explanation.surface: Someone drawing a flag and being told it is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' and 'flag' both look like nouns or art verbs; one is a sporting result and the other means to weaken.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw in a match is a tie: both mean a result where neither side wins.

clue.text: I've no other words to end with

indicators.note: other means different, so the letters are made into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A speaker admitting they have nothing more to say to finish with.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoi is a short closing stanza of a poem or the concluding words of a book.

clue.text: House with a bad character? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means half of the word is dropped, so the second five of its ten letters go

parts.note: villainous means wicked, having the character of a villain

explanation.surface: A home with a disreputable occupant, followed by the British exclamation 'not half!' meaning 'absolutely!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'you bet!', but here it removes half of VILLAINOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large country or holiday residence, a kind of house.

clue.text: Washington letters read out with lines cut — don't believe them

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so the two letters are said as their names, dee-see

parts.note: DC, District of Columbia, is the letters after Washington

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a verse is a set of lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A warning about letters from the US capital being read with lines removed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter names D and C, spoken together, sound like the first two syllables; VERSE without its last letter supplies the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceivers are liars and tricksters, people whose words should not be trusted.

clue.text: Fellow journalist's triumph

parts.note: ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist
to triumph is to win

explanation.surface: A colleague celebrating a reporter's success.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin is a man's name, and a crossword fellow is any man.

clue.text: Spokesperson's crap can annoy weekly, liberal admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the liberal letter goes inside the jumble
crap means bad, so the letters are badly arranged and need reordering

explanation.surface: A press spokesperson's nonsense can irritate a liberal weekly paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crap' rearranges CAN ANNOY WEEKLY, and 'admitted' puts L inside. The 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kellyanne Conway was counselor to President Trump and spoke for his administration on TV.

clue.text: Annoys Sweden to no purpose

parts.note: needles means irritates or provokes
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Someone irritating the Swedes for no reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means unnecessary, done without any point or reason.

clue.text: Doing as one's asked — endless bilge going out

indicators.note: out means not in proper order, so the remaining letters are shuffled
endless says each of the two words loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Getting rid of the bilge water on request, as a dutiful sailor might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the last letter from each word, giving BILG and GOIN; 'out' rearranges those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Obliging means accommodating, readily helping when someone makes a request.

clue.text: Short of money, shafted you and me for capital

indicators.note: shafted means badly treated or wrecked, so the letters are scrambled
short of means lacking, so the money letter comes out

explanation.surface: A complaint that the two of us were cheated out of our cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of' removes M from YOU AND ME, and 'shafted' rearranges the remaining letters. 'capital' means capital city, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaoundé is the capital city of Cameroon.

clue.text: Show fake news regularly, including lies one's forgotten

parts.note: a sham is a fake

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so the two letters go around what is left of lies
regularly takes every other letter of news
forgotten means left out, so the letter for one goes

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A demand to broadcast fake news at intervals, lies included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a verb but is the definition: Shameless is a British TV drama about a chaotic Manchester family.
explanation.definitionFit: Shameless is a Channel 4 comedy-drama series, later remade in the US.

clue.text: Poor Sean's finally left (extremely sensible)

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the letters are rearranged
finally takes the closing letter of left

explanation.surface: Poor Sean has gone, and was very level-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanest is the superlative of sane, meaning most rational or level-headed.

clue.text: No director puts down what thespian does

indicators.note: no says the director letter is absent, so it is removed

parts.note: demotes means puts down to a lower rank

explanation.surface: An actor carrying on when no director is there to keep them in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to express emotion theatrically, which is the stock thing an actor does.

clue.text: Tree French writer climbs

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upward, so the name is read bottom to top

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French author

explanation.surface: A French author scrambling up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a small tree or shrub, related to the cashew.

clue.text: Language that's somewhat lyrical (in gobbledygook)

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Song lyrics written in meaningless jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Language' alone; the draft included 'that's', which is a link word joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is an informal word for a language or jargon.

clue.text: Shooter's identity commonly in question, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means spoken out loud, so the sound of the question is what counts

parts.note: asking someone's identity is 'who's he?', and a common, h-dropping speaker says it as 'oo's 'e'

explanation.surface: Someone asking for the name of the gunman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' tells you to drop the h's, as some Cockney speakers do: 'who's he' becomes 'oo-zee'. The 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uzi is an Israeli submachine gun, so it is a type of firearm, a shooter in slang.

clue.text: Splendid hosts for Mike, all right?

indicators.note: hosts means holds within, so noble wraps around the word for for

parts.note: noble means grand or splendid
pro means in favour of, for
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A grand party for someone called Mike, checking everything is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No problem' is a casual reply meaning that's fine, matching all right as a reassurance.

clue.text: Speech's trouble — you can see through it

indicators.note: speech means spoken, so the word for trouble is heard rather than written

parts.note: pain means trouble, as in 'a pain to deal with'

explanation.surface: A speaker's difficulty is obvious to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A pane is a sheet of glass in a window, which is transparent.

clue.text: See 7
Honour, contrarily, the third for Conrad Black

indicators.note: contrarily means the opposite way, so the honour's letters are read backwards

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

indicators.note: the third takes the third letter of Conrad

explanation.surface: Conrad Black, the press baron, was given a peerage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conrad Black' looks like one name; it splits, with Black as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebon is a poetic word for the colour of ebony, meaning very dark.

clue.text: See 10
Excuse deception perpetrated

parts.note: a con is a trick or deception
done means carried out, as a deed is perpetrated

explanation.surface: Letting a fraud off the hook.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone is to overlook or forgive wrongdoing.
